longForm.overview:
🇺🇦 is the emoji of blue-and-yellow coded national-identity read — the blue-and-gold banner, the sunflower-blue coded flex, and the universal 'blue-and-yellow pulse' tag for Ukraine pride. Where 🇺🇳 reads as neutral-coded diplomacy read and 🏳️‍🌈 reads as rainbow-coded pride read, 🇺🇦 captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate blue-and-yellow coded identity — a 'blue-and-yellow 🇺🇦' heritage check-in or a 'sunflower-blue pulse 🇺🇦' Zhovto-Blakytni reveal. The blue-and-gold banner cue borrows from Ukraine's national flag tradition and the modern heritage-coded aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as blue-and-yellow coded rather than literal travel-coded flag.

In real-world usage 🇺🇦 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate blue-and-yellow energy. A partner sends it on a 'blue-and-yellow 🇺🇦' heritage check-in. A friend sends it on a 'sunflower-blue pulse 🇺🇦' pride reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'blue-and-yellow coded 🇺🇦' heritage-month thread. The blue-and-gold banner cue is what makes the emoji feel blue-and-yellow coded — it is not just 'flag,' it is 'blue-and-yellow coded Ukraine-pride moment.'

What separates 🇺🇦 from the rest of the flag family is the blue-and-yellow register. The emoji is not saying 'rainbow pride' (🏳️‍🌈), 'black rebellion' (🏴), or 'checkered finish' (🏁). It is saying 'blue-and-yellow coded Ukraine-coded identity,' which carries a specific national-flag tradition. That is why 🇺🇦 travels especially well on partner heritage check-ins, Zhovto-Blakytni reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with blue-and-yellow energy.

longForm.whenNotToUse:
